# Scheduling and Webhook Triggers

Covers dimensions 6 (Scheduling) and 8 (Webhook support). All citations
reference entries in [citations.md](../citations.md).

---

## Scheduling

### Cron Support

Tines supports cron expressions for scheduling actions, introduced December
2022 [26]. The UI provides common patterns ("every day at 9am", "once a
week") with an option to enter custom cron syntax [26].

### Interval Limits

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| Minimum interval | 1 minute (60 seconds) | [38] |
| Maximum interval | Monthly | [38] |
| Default schedule | 09:00 AM in tenant default timezone | [26] |

### Timezone Handling

- Configurable timezone per scheduled action [discovery findings]
- `DATE("now")` function returns UTC by default [discovery findings]
- Timezone conversion via tz database values [discovery findings]
- Default: tenant's configured timezone

### Implementation

Uses sidekiq-scheduler Ruby gem internally. Configuration stored as cron
syntax in database. Sidekiq processes scheduled jobs (est., from discovery
findings).

## Webhook Support

### Incoming Webhooks

Webhook actions listen for incoming HTTP requests and convert payloads to
Tines events [16].

### URL Structure

Standard: `https://<tenant>.tines.com/webhook/<path>/<secret>` [16]

Response-enabled: `https://<tenant>.tines.com/api/public/<api-path-prefix>` [34]

### Authentication Methods

| Method | Description | Source |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| Secret in URL | Random token appended to webhook path (default) | [16] |
| HMAC-SHA256 signing | `<timestamp>.<webhook_url>.<request_body>` | [16] |
| OAuth | Team or Tenant scoped access | [16] |
| API keys | Bearer or Basic via Authorization header | [16][35] |
| Public (no auth) | Secret can be removed | [16] |

### HTTP Methods

Configurable via `verbs` parameter as comma-separated values (e.g.,
`"get,post"`) [16].

### Payload Handling

- JSON arrays, booleans, strings wrapped in `{"_json": ...}` object [16]
- Headers normalized: dashes → underscores, lowercase [16]
- Raw body capture via `capture_raw_body` option [16]
- Include/exclude headers via `include_headers` (default: true) [16]
- Webhook payload size limit: 30 MB [21]

### Request Filtering

Matching rules using `field==value` syntax against headers or body fields
with dot notation paths. `must_match` parameter controls how many rules
must pass [16].

### Rate Limiting

| Parameter | Limit | Source |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| Per webhook path | 1,000 requests/min | [36] |
| Per tenant | 2,500 requests/min | [36] |
| Custom rate limiting | Configurable key/count/period | [37] |
| Exceed behavior | HTTP 429 | [16][37] |

### Custom Responses

Three configurable elements [16]:
- **response**: Message text, resource data, or redirect URL
- **response_code**: HTTP status (default 201)
- **response_headers**: Custom headers object

Responses can reference incoming request data via `<<headers.*>>` or
`<<body.*>>` [16].

### Response-Enabled Webhooks

- 100 concurrent responses (1,000 for dedicated tenants) [16]
- 30-second timeout to reach an Exit action [16][34]
- X-Tines-Status header: `data_received` or `ok` [34]
- X-Tines-Response-Location for async result retrieval [34]
- HTTP 201 Created when concurrent limit exceeded [34]

## Gaps and Limitations

- **No sub-minute scheduling** — minimum 1 minute interval [38]
- **Webhook custom domains** — mentioned but implementation details not
  found in fetched content
- **Webhook payload limit** — 30 MB max [21]
- **Response-enabled webhook concurrency** — limited to 100 (or 1,000)
  concurrent responses [16]
